boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of San Francisco, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm first-weekend sequence that begins on the Hilltop, makes space for campus resources and activity, then heads into nearby public San Francisco destinations.

cards.title: 1. Get oriented on the Hilltop
cards.subtitle: Start with the USF walking-tour route
cards.notes: Use USF’s published walking-tour map to spot the library, University Center, church, recreation center, and athletics buildings before making separate plans.
cards.short_summary: Build a visual mental map of the main campus first.
cards.evidence_claim: USF’s walking-tour map identifies 21 campus destinations, including Gleeson Library, Koret Health and Recreation Center, St. Ignatius Church, University Center, and War Memorial Gym.
cards.access_notes: Follow posted campus access guidance; this map is a wayfinding resource.

cards.title: 2. Find your study base
cards.subtitle: Main campus library
cards.notes: Walk through Gleeson and identify a quiet seat or group-study option. Save the library’s research-help contact for the first assignment that needs it.
cards.short_summary: A practical stop for study space and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: USF describes Gleeson Library | Geschke Center as a place for research, discovery, collaboration, quiet study, group-study rooms, and library services.
cards.access_notes: Library services and spaces are intended for the USF community; check current building access before visiting.

cards.title: 3. Locate the student hub
cards.subtitle: USF main campus
cards.notes: Pass through the University Center and note its location on your map. It is a useful anchor when meeting classmates or finding student-facing offices.
cards.short_summary: Use a central campus landmark as a meeting point.
cards.evidence_claim: USF’s walking-tour map lists the University Center as a named destination on the Hilltop campus.
cards.access_notes: Check posted building access and office hours before relying on a specific service.

cards.title: 4. Pause at St. Ignatius Church
cards.subtitle: Named stop on USF’s Hilltop campus
cards.notes: Add the church to your campus loop for a quiet landmark visit. Keep to open public areas and respect any service, event, or restoration notices.
cards.short_summary: A campus landmark for a reflective break.
cards.evidence_claim: USF’s campus-experience page identifies St. Ignatius Church as part of the Hilltop campus, and the university walking-tour map includes it as a stop.
cards.source_title: The Campus Experience | University of San Francisco
cards.access_notes: Access may be affected by worship services, special events, or building work; follow on-site notices.

cards.title: 5. Check out campus recreation
cards.subtitle: USF recreation and wellness facility
cards.notes: Locate Koret and review the recreation options available to USF students. Choose a future class, open-recreation period, or intramural activity that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: Connect campus orientation with a sustainable wellness routine.
cards.evidence_claim: USF says Koret offers fitness facilities, classes, wellness programs, intramural sports, personal training, and recreation opportunities.
cards.access_notes: USF identifies Koret as open to students, faculty, staff, alumni, and members; confirm current eligibility and facility hours.

cards.title: 6. Put one campus event on your calendar
cards.subtitle: USF student-run programming
cards.notes: Look for a Campus Activities Board event or student-organization meeting that genuinely interests you. Bring a classmate so the first conversation has an easy start.
cards.short_summary: Turn orientation into an actual campus connection.
cards.evidence_claim: USF states that the Campus Activities Board is a student-run organization that plans and coordinates on-campus entertainment.
cards.source_title: Campus Activities Board | University of San Francisco
cards.access_notes: Programming varies by term; consult USF’s current event information for dates and attendance details.

cards.entity_name: War Memorial Gym at the Sobrato Center
cards.title: 7. See a Dons venue
cards.subtitle: USF athletics facility
cards.notes: Find the gym on your campus route and check the official athletics calendar later for an age-appropriate home event that works with your first few weeks.
cards.short_summary: Learn where a visible part of campus spirit happens.
cards.evidence_claim: USF’s campus-experience page describes cheering Dons basketball teams at War Memorial Gym at the Sobrato Center.
cards.source_title: The Campus Experience | University of San Francisco
cards.access_notes: Event admission, schedules, and access rules vary; verify the specific event with USF Athletics before going.

cards.title: 8. Take an afternoon park walk
cards.subtitle: Buena Vista and Haight, San Francisco
cards.notes: Use daylight hours for a short walk on the park’s marked trails, then pause at an upper-slope viewpoint. Stay on established paths and go with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A nearby outdoor reset with city views.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks describes Buena Vista Park as the city’s oldest park, with winding trails, coast live oaks, and views from its upper slopes.
cards.source_title: Buena Vista Park | San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: Official park hours are 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; visit in daylight and follow posted park rules.

cards.title: 9. Ride the park shuttle
cards.subtitle: Golden Gate Park’s JFK Promenade route
cards.notes: Use the official free shuttle to connect a few Golden Gate Park destinations without trying to cover the whole park on foot. Check the schedule before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A low-cost way to sample several park landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks says the Golden Gate Park Shuttle is free, runs daily, and stops at museums, gardens, and the Conservatory of Flowers.
cards.source_title: Golden Gate Park Free Shuttle | San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: Official service runs 9 a.m.–6 p.m. on weekends and holidays, and noon–6 p.m. weekdays; check for updates before travel.

cards.title: 10. End at the Japanese Tea Garden
cards.subtitle: Golden Gate Park, 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Drive
cards.notes: Finish the weekend with a slow garden walk and a few photos of the pagoda and landscape. Arrive early on a listed free-hour day if that timing suits you.
cards.short_summary: A clear final destination for a quieter Sunday outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Gardens of Golden Gate Park lists the Japanese Tea Garden at 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Drive and offers a free hour Monday, Wednesday, and Friday from 9–10 a.m.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admissions | Gardens of Golden Gate Park
cards.access_notes: The garden is open daily; last entry changes seasonally. The documented free hour is Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, 9–10 a.m.
